title: A Homecoming for the Scholarship
premise: Felix Vane, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, has spent three years pretending to belong — until the senior college essay prompt, 'What is the truest thing you know?', unlocks a vault of anonymous confessions that exposes the town's founding tradition as a cover for stolen land and erased families. When the essay archive threatens to close and bury the truth forever, Felix — whose own family was one of those erased — must decide whether exposing it will cost them the scholarship, the friends, and the fragile identity they've built. With help from Wren, the headmaster's daughter who chose them over her duty, Felix races to restore the archive before graduation, ending with the truth read aloud at commencement: the academy survives, but remade on honest ground, and Felix finally stops saying they're fine.
about_author: Zephyrine Hartwell is a former boarding school archivist who writes stories about the secrets institutions keep and the teenagers who refuse to. She lives in a converted chapel with too many books and one judgmental cat.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At Hollowmere Academy, the annual senior essay prompt is posted: 'What is the truest thing you know?' Felix drafts a safe, polished lie about belonging. But classmates begin submitting raw, dangerous truths anonymously to the old confession archive in the library basement. Emotional beat: the ache of performing a self.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (A Rehearsal)
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A scholarship review meeting reminds Felix how conditional their place is. They tour campus with best friend Priya, cataloguing all the ways they've learned to pass. That night, curious about the archive's sudden activity, Felix finds the basement door unlocked. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as gratitude.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The headmaster's daughter manages the archive as her family duty, sealing each year's essays unread. She's read this year's early entries — including one describing the Founders' Trust, which 'gave' the academy its land. She recognizes a name in it: Vane. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking under knowledge.

chapters.title: The Land Under the Lawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix and Wren secretly compare notes in the archive stacks. Deeds, ledgers, and a 1920s photograph reveal the academy was built on farmland taken from families like Felix's, renamed and forgotten. Emotional beat: history turning personal; fury arriving quietly.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Headmaster Aldous discovers the archive has been accessed and warns Wren that opening sealed essays violates the Trust's charter — the legal mechanism that keeps donors funding the school. He offers her his role someday if she lets it go. Emotional beat: love against duty, offered as inheritance.

chapters.title: Confessions We Didn't Write
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Anonymous essays start appearing publicly — photocopied, slipped into lockers. The school fractures: some students demand the archive be burned, others hunger for more. Priya realizes Felix is involved and feels betrayed by the secrecy. Emotional beat: friendship strained by chosen risks.

chapters.title: The Sealing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The board votes to seal the archive permanently and destroy unsubmitted essays before commencement. Felix learns their own admission was funded by the very Trust built on their family's loss — the scholarship was hush money wearing a bow. Emotional beat: identity collapsing into a single terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Nineteen days until destruction. Wren chooses Felix over her father, copying the charter and finding a loophole: the Trust requires one public reading of the archive every fifty years — and the last one never happened. Emotional beat: duty inverted into a weapon of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At graduation, Wren invokes the reading clause from the stage while Felix and Priya hold the board at bay with copied documents and donor pressure. Felix reads the founding families' names aloud, ending with their own. The board, cornered by law and witnesses alike, cannot stop it. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: The Truest Thing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Weeks later: the academy announces a restorative commission, land acknowledgments become policy, and Felix's scholarship is rewritten as an endowed fund in their family's name. Wren and Felix stand in the open archive door, no longer hiding anything. Asked if they're fine, Felix finally says what's true. Emotional beat: homecoming — not to a place, but to a self.
